units.title: Construct: Lazy fused pull pipelines and typed early termination
steps: Derive evaluation order, consumption and side effects for filter-even/map-square/take, and distinguish external next from an internal fold with typed break.
Implement co_next, co_flow_next and co_fold without an iterator library, then build an unfused equivalent and compare exact source-pull and callback counts before timing.
checks: range0..10, step1, take3 emits0,4,16 after1,3,5 source pulls; the next call returns DONE without a sixth pull. Breaking after two outputs leaves16 as the next output.

Enumerate half-open ranges, nonunit steps, empty take, exhaustion and early break against a materialized mathematical oracle. Check UINT16-edge squaring and resumed iteration; reject extra-pull-after-take and skipped-map mutants.

units.title: Construct: Volcano scan/filter/group operators with pull backpressure
steps: Explain open/next/close and group-boundary ownership in a pull dataflow plan; distinguish iterator backpressure from unbounded eager materialization.
Implement the fused contiguous-key nonnegative-sum query, an unfused scan/filter/group operator chain and a bounded push adapter with identical error and order contracts.
checks: Rows(1,-1),(1,3),(1,4),(2,-8),(3,5),(4,6) produce(1,7),(3,5),(4,6). A first next stops at index3 and cannot consume group3.

Compare all short key/value streams against an independent grouping oracle, including negative-only groups, overflow, repeated keys separated by another group, early close and output canaries. Reject negative-value inclusion and consuming-later-groups mutants.
reasoning: Explain open/next/close and group-boundary ownership in a pull dataflow plan; distinguish iterator backpressure from unbounded eager materialization.

steps: Derive frame state, suspension lifetime, allocation failure and destruction rules; distinguish compiler-generated C++ coroutine storage from an explicit C frame.

Implement the factorial0..12 frame with a bounded multiplier stack, one-transition budgets, stable completion and cancellation, without recursive calls or tail-call optimization assumptions.
checks: factorial6 takes14 single-transition steps: six pushes, one base transition, six pops and one completion. Output stays91 until completion then becomes720.

Compare factorial values with Python integers for every admitted n and every budget partition, including budget0 and cancellation at each state. Assert maximum depth and output publication; reject zero-base and omitted-multiplication mutants.
reasoning: Transform recursive factorial into continuation-passing form and then a finite continuation representation, explaining which control and environment values were made explicit.
deliverables: Implement the factorial0..12 frame with a bounded multiplier stack, one-transition budgets, stable completion and cancellation, without recursive calls or tail-call optimization assumptions.

Compare factorial values with Python integers for every admitted n and every budget partition, including budget0 and cancellation at each state. Assert maximum depth and output publication; reject zero-base and omitted-multiplication mutants.

units.title: Construct: Readiness-based async frames and the register/recheck race
steps: Explain readiness as a hint, partial progress as frame state, and registration/quiescence lifetime; distinguish this model from completion submission rings and automatic Rust Future pinning.

Implement exact-length asynchronous reads with at most two reads per poll, arm-then-recheck, generation-scoped notifications, synchronous disarm and cancelled/error terminal states. Build an io.reactor/io.stream/io.deadline adapter.
checks: The fake reader returns AGAIN until arm, then supplies all three bytes on the immediate recheck: one poll completes after2 reads,1 arm,1 disarm. A stale generation cannot mark the next frame ready.

Script readiness arriving between the first AGAIN and arm, repeated spurious wakeups, short progress plus ERROR, EOF, stale notifications and cancel. Preserve final output until complete and count all callbacks; reject omitted recheck and omitted disarm mutants.
reasoning: Explain readiness as a hint, partial progress as frame state, and registration/quiescence lifetime; distinguish this model from completion submission rings and automatic Rust Future pinning.
deliverables: Implement exact-length asynchronous reads with at most two reads per poll, arm-then-recheck, generation-scoped notifications, synchronous disarm and cancelled/error terminal states. Build an io.reactor/io.stream/io.deadline adapter.
